summary: Anton Shumskikh is named on the Form D for Neo Agent Inc., a London-located corporation incorporated in 2025 that has sold a $2.74M round to 13 investors, including Lookout Ventures I (S1, S3). The website likely belonging to the company (neoagent.io, guessed from the name and not confirmed) describes an AI agent that works IT service desk tickets end to end for managed service providers (MSPs). It shows approval gates, per-tool permissions, action logging, SOC 2 Type 2, a claim of 250+ MSP customers, a Pax8 Marketplace listing and weekly releases (S4, S5, S7). The auditability design and shipping pace echo the fund's beliefs, but the customer base is IT MSPs, not healthcare, insurance or financial services, and there is no evidence of the founders' backgrounds, so this looks off-thesis unless the founders show a regulated-industry angle.

company.what_they_build: An AI agent that works IT service desk tickets for MSPs, such as onboarding, password resets, triage, dispatch, RMM scripts and after-hours phone calls. It runs across the PSA, RMM, documentation and Microsoft stack, with technician approval rules, None/Read/Write permissions per tool and every action logged. Technicians can also use it as a teammate inside Microsoft Teams. This description comes from the unconfirmed neoagent.io site (S4, S5, S6, S7).

thesis_fit.belief: Compliance and auditability are the moat in regulated AI, not the model
thesis_fit.evidence: The product centres on approval gating, per-tool permissions, tenant isolation, action logging and SOC 2 Type 2. However, its customers are IT MSPs, not a regulated vertical, and the site link is unconfirmed.

thesis_fit.belief: Founders from inside the industry beat generalists who discover it later
thesis_fit.evidence: Nothing describes Shumskikh's or Sehgal's backgrounds. The site's 'Built by MSP people' claim would mean insiders to IT services, not to healthcare, insurance or financial services.

thesis_fit.belief: Open-source or public traction is the best early signal for technical founders
thesis_fit.evidence: There is no open-source or GitHub evidence. Public commercial traction is claimed (250+ MSPs, named case studies, Pax8 listing), but it sits on an unconfirmed website.

thesis_fit.belief: Small teams shipping weekly beat large early rounds
thesis_fit.evidence: The blog shows near-weekly releases with dozens of new integrations each, and the round is a modest $2.74M. Team size is unknown.

strengths: The auditability-first product design (approval rules, per-tool None/Read/Write permissions, logged actions, SOC 2 Type 2) matches the fund's view of what makes enterprise AI deployable (S4, S5).
Visible commercial traction: a claimed 250+ MSP customers, quantified case studies (Plus 1 Technology, Digacore) and Pax8 Marketplace distribution (S4, S5).
High shipping velocity, with weekly product updates and a rebuilt integration layer adding several integrations a week (S5).
Capital-efficient seed of $2.74M fully sold, with an institutional backer (Lookout Ventures I) (S1, S3).
risks: Off-thesis vertical: customers are IT MSPs, not healthcare, insurance or financial services (S4, S2).
The website was guessed from the company name. No page names Shumskikh or Sehgal, so the product, traction and SOC 2 claims are not confirmed to belong to the Form D filer (S4–S7).
There is no evidence about the founders' backgrounds, prior companies or technical depth, and the akta.pro profile is empty (S8).

The round looks largely closed: fully sold with 13 investors. The earlier screening also says Lookout Ventures holds a director seat, but only S2 makes that claim and the Form D record shows only 'backed_by'. Entry may be late or crowded for a pre-seed/seed fund (S1, S3, S2).
Crowded competitive set with named rivals Rewst, Pia, Thread, MSPBots and Zofiq (S4).
Hiring a Chief Marketing Officer focused on the MSP channel suggests the company is committing to the MSP market rather than moving toward regulated verticals (S5).
open_questions: What are your and Nikhil Sehgal's roles and backgrounds, and is neoagent.io your company?
The footer says 'Built by MSP people'. Who on the founding team ran or worked at an MSP, and which one?
How many of the 250+ MSPs pay, versus being on trial, and what does revenue look like after the Pax8 Marketplace launch?
Do any of your MSP customers serve healthcare, insurance or financial-services clients? Have HIPAA, FINRA or similar requirements come up in their deployments?
How do approval rules and action logs hold up in a customer's own audit? Has an MSP used Neo's logs as audit evidence?
When customers raise autonomy after test mode, what share of tickets does Neo close without a technician approval?
Is the $2.74M round closed, who leads it, and is there room for a new seed investor?
How large is the team shipping the weekly releases and the rebuilt integration layer?
conversation_openers: Congrats on the Pax8 Marketplace launch. Letting MSPs buy Neo through their existing Pax8 billing is a smart distribution move, and I'd love to hear how it has changed your trial-to-paid conversion.

Your per-tool None/Read/Write permissions and approval-gated actions are the kind of audit trail we look for in AI for regulated industries. I'm curious whether MSPs serving healthcare or finance clients are pulling you in that direction.

The Plus 1 Technology story, with triage dropping from 15 minutes to 2 and roughly two technicians' time saved daily, is a striking result. I'd love to understand what made that rollout work and how repeatable it is.
